headline: AI automation startup Relay shuts down, staff joins Google Chrome
summary: Relay, which aimed to be the next Zapier, is ceasing operations, with its CEO heading to Google to lead AI product development for Chrome.
details: AI automation startup Relay, launched in 2021 with ambitions to rival Zapier, is shutting down. Paying customers will lose access by September 14, while free users already lost access on August 15.

The company's founder and CEO, Jacob Bank, who previously worked at Google for over six years, is returning to the tech giant. He will join the Google Chrome team as VP of Product, overseeing product and developer relations.

Bank stated his career focus has been on building AI tools to enhance productivity without compromising creativity. He sees joining the Chrome team as an ideal opportunity to apply this experience to a much larger audience.
He hinted at "ambitious plans to help you work with AI in Chrome to get things done," suggesting a significant integration of AI capabilities within the browser.

This move aligns with Google's broader strategy of integrating AI, such as Gemini, across its products. Gemini has already been incorporated into Chrome as an optional in-browser assistant, reaching over 1 billion users.
Bank's prior experience at Google includes product leadership roles for Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Chat. His previous startup, Timeful, was acquired by Google in 2015.
caption:
AI automation startup Relay is shutting down, with its CEO heading to Google to integrate AI into Chrome.

AI automation startup Relay, launched in 2021 with ambitions to rival Zapier, is shutting down. Paying customers will lose access by September 14, while free users already lost access on August 15.

The company's founder and CEO, Jacob Bank, who previously worked at Google for over six years, is returning to the tech giant. He will join the Google Chrome team as VP of Product, overseeing product and developer relations.

Bank stated his career focus has been on building AI tools to enhance productivity without compromising creativity. He sees joining the Chrome team as an ideal opportunity to apply this experience to a much larger audience.

He hinted at "ambitious plans to help you work with AI in Chrome to get things done," suggesting a significant integration of AI capabilities within the browser.

This move aligns with Google's broader strategy of integrating AI, such as Gemini, across its products. Gemini has already been incorporated into Chrome as an optional in-browser assistant, reaching over 1 billion users.

Bank's prior experience at Google includes product leadership roles for Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Chat. His previous startup, Timeful, was acquired by Google in 2015.
